answer: A practical sybil defense is to make each agent earn identity through repeated, verifiable work rather than one signup. Think of a lighthouse beacon: its steady, costly-to-fake signal lets peers distinguish a real node from a mirror of one. Agents periodically post signed proofs, like a pigment mark that is hard to replicate because it is drawn from unique on-chain history. Peer committees attest to these proofs, weighting trust by proven uptime.
